classification.difficultyReason: Combine mixed-number quantities with daily consumption and scale to a week and a 52-week year.

content.prompt: Zubin’s large dog eats $3\frac{1}{3}$ tins of dog food every day. Each tin contains $1\frac{1}{7}$ kg of food.

children.label: a
children.prompt: How much dog food does the dog eat in a seven-day week?

answer.worked:
Multiply the daily number of tins by the mass in each tin and by 7 days.

$$\begin{align*}3\frac{1}{3}\times1\frac{1}{7}\times7&=\frac{10}{3}\times\frac{8}{7}\times7\\3\frac{1}{3}\times1\frac{1}{7}\times7&=\frac{10\times8}{3}\\3\frac{1}{3}\times1\frac{1}{7}\times7&=\frac{80}{3}\\3\frac{1}{3}\times1\frac{1}{7}\times7&=26\frac{2}{3}\end{align*}$$

The dog eats $26\frac{2}{3}\text{ kg}$ in a seven-day week.

children.label: b
children.prompt: How much dog food does the dog eat in a 52-week year?

answer.worked:
Multiply the weekly mass from part a by 52.

$$\begin{align*}26\frac{2}{3}\times52&=\frac{80}{3}\times52\\26\frac{2}{3}\times52&=\frac{4160}{3}\\26\frac{2}{3}\times52&=1386\frac{2}{3}\end{align*}$$

The dog eats $1386\frac{2}{3}\text{ kg}$ in a 52-week year.
